It watches metrics, containers and processes, and when something looks wrong it investigates: it correlates metrics, logs and events and explains the likely root cause in plain language. Free and MIT licensed; your data never leaves your servers. The landing page should send people to the GitHub repo and the docs.
"""

The decided foundation:
- surface (light or dark): Dark
- display-type (the heading typeface): IBM Plex Sans. Shown with the reason: Reads like engineering documentation: plain, steady, no decoration. Titles look precise on your dark page and sit well next to the GitHub and docs links you send people to.
- body-type (the body typeface): IBM Plex Sans. Shown with the reason: Same family as your heading, so the whole page reads as one system. Built for technical content, with clear digits that suit metrics and logs at 14-16px.
- type-scale (type size and weight): 16px body, headings ×1.25. Shown with the reason: Body text stays comfortable for root-cause explanations in plain language, while headings clearly separate sections. Good mix of dense data and easy reading on dark screens.
- brand-color (the brand colour): #28a4f0
- secondary-color (a supporting colour): #14b8a6. Shown with the reason: Clearly apart from your blue brand on a dark screen, so chart lines and secondary buttons stay easy to tell apart, and it does not clash with your green success colour.
- accent-color (an accent colour): #a78bfa. Shown with the reason: Your brand is blue and your supporting colour is teal, so violet reads as a third, rarer thing. Nothing in your green, amber or red status set is purple, so a badge can't be misread as a problem.
- neutral (the greys): Cool
- semantics (success/warning/error colours): #22c55e, #f59e0b, #ef4444
- spacing (density and spacing): Tight, 4px base. Shown with the reason: Your tool shows metrics, container lists and logs side by side. Small padding and small gaps mean more rows fit without scrolling, which is what someone watching servers all day wants.
- radius (corner rounding): Soft, 8px. Shown with the reason: A small 4px round matches your tight 4px spacing base, so corners and gaps feel like one system. Buttons and panels read as calm and modern without drawing attention away from your metrics and logs.
- depth (shadows and depth): Subtle. Shown with the reason: Cards, log panels and the GitHub link sit clearly above the page, so the eye groups them. Light enough to keep dense metric and container lists calm on dark grey.

reply.summary: Your foundation is built for a technical tool that people run on their own servers and read on a dark screen. Dark surface with cool greys keeps long metric, container and log views easy on the eyes, and one typeface throughout makes the page read as a single, trustworthy system. It points people cleanly to your GitHub repo and docs without decoration getting in the way.
reply.rule: Your blue brand colour (#28a4f0) is for identity and primary actions like the GitHub and docs links, while status colours stay reserved only for success, warning and error so a colour is never mistaken for a state.

reasons.surface: A dark background suits an always-on monitoring tool and makes your bright blue, teal and status colours stand out clearly, while keeping dense dashboards comfortable to watch for long stretches.
reasons.display-type: IBM Plex Sans gives headings the plain, precise feel of engineering docs, so titles look credible next to the GitHub and docs links you send people to.
reasons.body-type: Using the same family for body text keeps the page one system, and its clear digits read well for metrics, logs and root-cause explanations at 14-16px.
reasons.type-scale: 16px body keeps plain-language explanations easy to read, while headings at one and a quarter times that clearly split sections without wasting space.
reasons.brand-color: This blue is your one identity colour, so people learn that blue means you and your main links, which keeps the page recognisable across every screen.
reasons.secondary-color: Teal sits clearly apart from your blue on dark, so chart lines and secondary buttons stay easy to tell apart and never look like your green success colour.
reasons.accent-color: Violet is a rare third colour, so badges and highlights stand out without being confused with any green, amber or red status meaning.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys match the technical tone of your blue and teal and give dark panels a steady, even backdrop for dense metric and log lists.
reasons.semantics: Green, amber and red are used only for success, warning and error, so anyone scanning a dashboard reads system health correctly at a glance.
reasons.spacing: A tight 4px base with small padding fits more metric rows and containers on screen without scrolling, which is what someone watching servers all day wants.
reasons.radius: Soft 8px corners match your 4px spacing base, so buttons and panels feel like one calm, modern system without pulling attention from your data.
reasons.depth: Subtle shadows lift cards, log panels and the GitHub link just enough that the eye groups them, while keeping dense lists calm on the dark grey background.
